set.explanation: Warfarin is an anticoagulant: it inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, reducing synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X (and proteins C and S). Aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1, blocking thromboxane A2; clopidogrel irreversibly blocks the P2Y12 ADP receptor; and dipyridamole inhibits platelet phosphodiesterase and adenosine reuptake, raising cAMP. Antiplatelet drugs are used mainly against arterial (platelet-rich) thrombosis, whereas anticoagulants treat venous thromboembolism and prevent cardioembolic stroke in atrial fibrillation.

set.stem: Digoxin toxicity may be precipitated by all of the following EXCEPT:
set.explanation: Digoxin is excreted largely unchanged by the kidneys, so renal impairment — including the age-related fall in GFR and reduced lean body mass of older people — raises levels, whereas hepatic impairment has little effect. Hypokalaemia (e.g. from loop or thiazide diuretics), hypomagnesaemia, hypercalcaemia and hypothyroidism increase myocardial sensitivity, and drugs such as amiodarone, verapamil, clarithromycin and spironolactone raise digoxin levels. Toxicity causes nausea, xanthopsia, confusion and arrhythmias and, when severe, is treated with digoxin-specific antibody fragments.

set.stem: A 47-year-old man is admitted with an acute coronary syndrome. He has a history of peptic ulcer disease, and his cardiologist decides to use clopidogrel. What is the mechanism of action of clopidogrel?
options: Blocks ADP binding to its platelet P2Y12 receptor
set.explanation: Clopidogrel is a prodrug activated by hepatic CYP2C19 into a metabolite that irreversibly blocks the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor, preventing ADP-mediated activation of glycoprotein IIb/IIIa for the life of the platelet (7–10 days). Glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors (abciximab, eptifibatide, tirofiban) are intravenous drugs, dipyridamole is a non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor and sildenafil inhibits phosphodiesterase-5. Omeprazole and esomeprazole inhibit CYP2C19 and may reduce clopidogrel activation, so lansoprazole or pantoprazole is preferred for gastroprotection.

Loop diuretics block the Na⁺/K⁺/2Cl⁻ co-transporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, inhibiting sodium and chloride reabsorption so that water follows — the most potent diuresis of any class. The increased sodium delivery to the distal nephron enhances potassium and hydrogen ion secretion, causing hypokalaemia and metabolic alkalosis rather than a rise in potassium. Osmotic diuresis is produced by mannitol, and water-only diuresis (aquaresis) by vasopressin antagonists such as tolvaptan.

set.stem: In which of the following situations are beta-adrenoceptor antagonists (beta-blockers) indicated?
topics: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
set.explanation: Evidence-based beta-blockers (bisoprolol, carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, nebivolol) reduce mortality and hospitalisation by about a third in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; they are started at a low dose once the patient is euvolaemic and titrated slowly. Their negative inotropic and chronotropic effects make them harmful in acute decompensated left ventricular failure, cardiogenic shock and heart failure with bradycardia. High-output failure is managed by treating the underlying cause, such as anaemia, thyrotoxicosis or an arteriovenous fistula.

set.stem: A 71-year-old woman with hypertension presents with fatigue and rapid, irregular palpitations. She normally takes enalapril. Her pulse is irregularly irregular at 125 beats/min and her blood pressure is 128/86 mmHg; cardiovascular examination is otherwise normal. A 12-lead ECG shows atrial fibrillation with a poorly controlled ventricular rate and no other abnormality. Which of the following drugs is most suitable to control her heart rate?
set.explanation: For rate control of atrial fibrillation without heart failure or hypotension, a beta-blocker (e.g. bisoprolol) or a rate-limiting calcium-channel blocker (diltiazem, verapamil) is first line, aiming initially for a resting rate below 110 beats/min; digoxin is reserved for sedentary patients or added in combination. Amiodarone and flecainide are rhythm-control drugs (flecainide is contraindicated in structural or ischaemic heart disease), adenosine only transiently blocks the AV node and is used for re-entrant SVT, and lidocaine is for ventricular arrhythmias. She also needs stroke-risk assessment — her CHA₂DS₂-VASc score is 3 (age 65–74, female, hypertension) — and anticoagulation.

Oral anticoagulants reduce stroke and systemic embolism in non-valvular atrial fibrillation by about two-thirds, and the direct factor Xa inhibitor apixaban was more effective than warfarin with less major bleeding in the ARISTOTLE trial. Aspirin, alone or with clopidogrel, is not recommended for stroke prevention in AF because it is much less effective and carries a similar bleeding risk. Amiodarone and beta-blockers control rhythm or rate but do not prevent thromboembolism; anticoagulation is offered according to stroke risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc/CHA₂DS₂-VA score) weighed against bleeding risk.

Dipyridamole inhibits platelet phosphodiesterase and blocks adenosine reuptake, raising intracellular cAMP and inhibiting aggregation; modified-release dipyridamole with aspirin is an option for secondary stroke prevention when clopidogrel is not tolerated. Clopidogrel and prasugrel are irreversible thienopyridine P2Y12 blockers, ticagrelor is a reversible oral P2Y12 blocker, and cangrelor is an intravenous reversible P2Y12 blocker used during PCI. Cilostazol, used for intermittent claudication, is the other phosphodiesterase (PDE3) inhibitor with antiplatelet action.

set.stem: A 58-year-old man with known mitral valve prolapse presents with 4 weeks of fever, malaise and weight loss after a dental extraction. Transthoracic echocardiography shows a vegetation on his native mitral valve with no abscess, and he has no embolic complications. Blood cultures grow viridans streptococci fully sensitive to penicillin, and his renal function is normal. What is the most appropriate antibiotic regimen to start?
set.explanation: Native-valve endocarditis caused by penicillin-sensitive viridans streptococci is treated with intravenous benzylpenicillin (or amoxicillin or ceftriaxone) for 4 weeks, or for 2 weeks combined with gentamicin in uncomplicated cases with normal renal function; the synergistic penicillin–gentamicin combination is the classic UK regimen. Flucloxacillin targets Staphylococcus aureus, vancomycin with gentamicin is for penicillin allergy or resistant organisms, and broad-spectrum meropenem is unnecessary. Initial treatment must be intravenous; current ESC guidance allows a switch to oral therapy only after at least 10 days of IV antibiotics in stable patients.

set.stem: Which of the following beta-blockers has been shown to reduce mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)?
topics: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
set.explanation: Mortality reduction in HFrEF has been shown in large randomised trials for bisoprolol (CIBIS-II), carvedilol (COPERNICUS) and controlled-release metoprolol succinate (MERIT-HF). Short-acting metoprolol tartrate was inferior to carvedilol in COMET, bucindolol did not reduce mortality in BEST, and nebivolol reduced the combined endpoint of death or cardiovascular hospitalisation in older patients (SENIORS) but not mortality alone, so the benefit is not a pure class effect. Guidelines therefore recommend one of the evidence-based agents, started low and titrated to the target dose.

set.stem: All of the following drugs used in the acute management of ST-elevation myocardial infarction are correctly matched to their mechanism of benefit EXCEPT:
options: Abciximab – inhibition of the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor
Beta-adrenergic antagonists – reduced myocardial oxygen consumption
Clopidogrel – inhibition of the platelet adenosine diphosphate (ADP) receptor
set.explanation: Nitroglycerin (glyceryl trinitrate) releases nitric oxide and acts mainly as a venodilator, lowering preload and ventricular wall stress, with some coronary vasodilatation; afterload falls only at higher doses, so its principal benefit is preload reduction. Aspirin irreversibly inhibits COX-1 and thromboxane A2 production, abciximab blocks glycoprotein IIb/IIIa, beta-blockers lower heart rate and contractility and therefore myocardial oxygen demand, and clopidogrel blocks the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor. Nitrates are avoided in hypotension, right ventricular infarction and after recent phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor use.

NSAIDs such as ibuprofen inhibit renal prostaglandin synthesis, causing sodium and water retention and loss of prostaglandin-mediated vasodilatation, which blunts the effect of ACE inhibitors, ARBs and diuretics. The combination of an ACE inhibitor or ARB, a diuretic and an NSAID (the 'triple whammy') also risks acute kidney injury and hyperkalaemia. Paracetamol and allopurinol do not antagonise ACE inhibitors, chlorpromazine tends to lower blood pressure, and spironolactone adds to the antihypertensive effect (with a risk of hyperkalaemia).

set.stem: A 48-year-old woman who has been treated for essential hypertension for 3 months presents with a persistent dry cough that has not responded to linctus or antibiotics. Which antihypertensive is most likely responsible?
set.explanation: ACE inhibitors cause a dry, non-productive cough in about 10–15% of patients because blocking ACE (kininase II) prevents breakdown of bradykinin and substance P in the airways. The cough may begin weeks to months after starting treatment, does not respond to linctus or antibiotics, and resolves within 1–4 weeks of stopping; switching to an ARB, which does not affect bradykinin, is the usual solution. Amlodipine typically causes ankle oedema, thiazide and loop diuretics cause electrolyte disturbance, and atenolol causes fatigue and cold peripheries.

Dipyridamole is a phosphodiesterase inhibitor that also blocks cellular adenosine reuptake; the resulting rise in platelet cAMP inhibits aggregation, and modified-release dipyridamole with aspirin is recommended after TIA or ischaemic stroke when clopidogrel is not tolerated. Glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors (tirofiban, eptifibatide) block fibrinogen cross-linking of platelets and P2Y12 inhibitors (clopidogrel, ticagrelor) block ADP-mediated activation. Glycoprotein Ib (the von Willebrand factor receptor) and glycoprotein VI (the collagen receptor) are not targets of drugs in routine use.

Tirofiban, like eptifibatide and abciximab, blocks the platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor — the final common pathway of aggregation — preventing fibrinogen from cross-linking platelets; it is now used mainly as bail-out therapy during PCI (e.g. large thrombus burden or no-reflow). Aspirin inhibits thromboxane A2 production, heparins activate antithrombin III, nitrates are vasodilators, and bivalirudin is a reversible direct thrombin inhibitor.

Clarithromycin is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that markedly increases simvastatin levels, risking myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, so simvastatin should be withheld for the duration of the course. Aspirin and clopidogrel have no clinically important interaction with clarithromycin, and the QT-prolonging and serotonergic concerns with amitriptyline and tramadol call for caution rather than stopping them. Doxycycline is an alternative for cellulitis in penicillin allergy that avoids this interaction.
